fact_sheet.business_description: the Company provides a travel-payments franchise and financial-services activities including banking [D01]. The business links cardholders, merchants, and a service promise, generating income through service charges and the utilization of funds held between receipt and settlement [D01].
products_customers_and_why_they_buy: Charge-card services sold to cardholders and merchants; the product is a promise to pay, relying on customer confidence and merchant acceptance [D01].
economics: Pretax margins for travel-related services, investment/advisory services, and banking were approximately 14.6%, 19.8%, and 17.3% respectively in Q2 1994 [D06].
Travel-related services ROE was 23.8% in Q2 1994 versus 12.2% in Q2 1993; bank ROE was 10.03% versus 11.97% [D06].
Pricing power is tested by the seller's ability to maintain prices amid competitive pressure on merchant charges, cardholder benefits, and funding costs [D01].
earnings_record: Cyclicality is present due to reliance on travel payments and financial service activities which depend on market conditions [D01], [D05].
competitive_position: The company possesses a recognized travel-payments brand [D01].
Competes with bank-issued payment networks through acceptance, pricing, and cardholder benefits [D06].
Market share and peer rankings not in pack.
balance_sheet_and_capital_needs: Year-end 1993: Cash $3,312 million; Short + long debt $21,050 million; Equity $8,734 million [D02].
Bank Tier-1 capital 6.6% and total capital 13.0% as of Q2 1994 [D06].
Requires funds to manage redemption, settlement, and credit obligations [D01].
management_and_capital_allocation: Management is refocusing on payments and financial-services franchises and moving away from an unfocused conglomerate strategy [D01], [D03].
Insider ownership and specific incentives not in pack.
price_and_valuation: P/B: 2.24x (based on 1993 pro-forma book value of $11.81) [D04].
what_the_market_is_worried_about: Competitive card networks and merchant resistance to fees [D05].
Difficulty of reversing an unfocused conglomerate strategy [D05].
Potential impairment of trust in the payments service due to losses in separate activities [D01].
deal_terms_if_any: Original 1991 preferred investment: $300 million principal, 8.85% coupon ($26.55 million annual), convertible with value capped at $414 million [D02].
recent_events: July 25, 1994: Q2 results released showing revenue net of interest up 6.4% and continuing EPS up 16.7% compared to Q2 1993 [D03].
berkshire_context: Berkshire holds a pre-existing preferred interest [D02], [D07].
Opportunity cost exists relative to other potential franchise investments [D08].
document_conflicts: FY1993 net income of $1,478 million [D02] vs pro-forma book value adjustments [D02]; consolidated equity $8,734 million vs pro-forma $11.81 per share [D02].
missing_data: Full current-year cash flow; current tangible-capital reconciliation; dated external peer valuation grid; August 1st market close; exact current issuer balance sheet.

understandable.evidence: The business operates a recognizable travel-payments franchise relying on customer confidence and merchant acceptance, a model that has remained stable [D01].

durable_moat_and_pricing_power.evidence: The company possesses a recognized travel-payments brand that serves as a network, though it must balance fees against competitive merchant and cardholder pressures [D01], [D06].

consistent_earnings_record.evidence: While historical net income fluctuated due to non-core divestments, the core payments franchise has demonstrated steady growth in continuing EPS, rising to $2.30 in 1993 [D02].

high_roe_little_debt.evidence: The core travel-related services segment achieved a 23.8% ROE in Q2 1994, and the banking unit maintains adequate capital ratios with Tier-1 capital at 6.6% [D06].

capital_intensity.evidence: The payments business is a service-oriented franchise that does not require heavy capital investment in property, plant, or equipment [D01].

able_honest_owner_minded_management.evidence: Management is actively refocusing the firm on its core payments and financial-services franchises, moving away from an unfocused, value-destructive conglomerate strategy [D01], [D03].

size_moves_the_needle.evidence: With a market capitalization of approximately $13.12 billion, the company is of sufficient scale to be meaningful for Berkshire [D04].

price_screen.evidence: The earnings yield of 8.68% is attractive relative to the long-term bond environment typical for this era [D04].

conflicts_resolved: FY1993 net income vs pro-forma book value: Relying on 1993 continuing EPS of $2.30 as the most accurate reflection of the core franchise's normalized earnings power [D02].
gate1.one_line_business_quality_verdict: a powerful travel-payments franchise regaining its focus and earning high returns on tangible capital.

gate2.why_available: The market is overly pessimistic about the company's ability to shed its conglomerate past and maintain its travel-payments moat against competition. Mr. Market is mispricing the franchise by focusing on temporary volatility in earnings and the structural complexity of the transition, rather than the core payments economics [D01], [D05]. As management continues to simplify the firm and core earnings growth resumes, the intrinsic value of the payments network will become increasingly apparent [D03].
evidence: 1993 continuing EPS of $2.30 demonstrates the underlying earning power of the core franchise [D02].
Q2 1994 results indicate revenue growth and a 16.7% increase in continuing EPS, signaling the franchise's resilience [D03].
The market remains fixated on competitive pressures and legacy conglomerate concerns, obscuring the high 23.8% ROE in the travel-related services segment [D05], [D06].
gate2.market_narrative_we_disagree_with: The market believes the travel-payments franchise is in permanent decline due to merchant fee resistance and competition, and that the company is too damaged by past diversification to recover [D05].
what_must_be_true: The core travel-payments network maintains its essential value to merchants and cardholders despite fee competition.
Management successfully completes the divestiture of non-core, value-destructive assets.
The company's credit loss experience remains within manageable historical bounds.
The competitive advantage of the brand and payment network remains intact.

key_assumptions: Core franchise earnings power remains at $2.30 per share [D02]
Divestiture of non-core assets successfully completed [D03]
Payments network maintains competitive moat against merchant fee pressure [D05]

gate3.price_vs_value: Price $26.50 is approx 115% of low-end value; limited margin of safety.
gate3.alternatives: Existing Berkshire holdings and potential treasury yields are safer; purchase of this equity offers less margin of safety than internal Berkshire capital allocation [D08].
gate3.downside_case: Continued failure to divest non-core segments and loss of pricing power in payments network; while potential for permanent loss exists if franchise is impaired, the preferred position offers seniority [D01], [D02].
flagged_assumptions: Discount rate of 7.5% assumed as representative of long-term government bond rate
Normalization of earnings based on 1993 continuing EPS

gate4.role_description: permanent_passive_holder — value realised by the business compounding and rational capital allocation; Berkshire's edge is patience and permanent capital [D02], [D07].
value_realisation_path: Earnings growth driven by the core payments franchise refocusing [D01], [D03].
Normalization of valuation multiples as the market recognizes the resilience of the travel-payments network [D05].
gate4.why_this_role_fits_the_era: For the 1980-1999 period, we seek to hold consumer franchises with sustainable moats for the long term; as a passive holder, we benefit from the business compounding its intrinsic value while management executes its strategy [D01], [D03].

kill_criteria: Pricing power lost to persistent merchant fee resistance and competitive bank networks [D01], [D05]
Management fails to complete the divestiture of non-core, value-destructive assets [D03]
Credit losses exceed manageable historical bounds impairing capital ratios [D06]
gate5.berkshire_constraints: Regulatory ownership thresholds and insurance capital requirements apply; we must remain mindful of the concentration of our existing preferred position [D02], [D07].
gate5.opportunity_cost: Existing Berkshire holdings and potential treasury yields offer higher certainty; current margin of safety is limited [D08].
gate5.decider_reason: The business is a well-understood consumer franchise within our circle of competence, and we already maintain a significant preferred position.
gate5.biggest_risk_in_one_sentence: The potential impairment of the core travel-payments franchise due to competitive pressures and failed execution of the strategic refocusing.

valuation.downside_case: Continued failure to divest non-core segments or significant loss of pricing power in the payments network [D01], [D02].

drivers.driver: Price vs value — the stock sells at a P/E of 11.52x, or an 8.68% initial earnings yield, against an appraised intrinsic value range of $23-$28 per share [D04].
The company operates a premier travel-payments franchise that remains essential to merchants and cardholders, providing a durable moat that persists despite competitive noise [D01], [D05].
Management is effectively refocusing the firm on its core payments and financial-services business, shedding the value-destructive conglomerate assets of the past [D01], [D03].
The core travel-related services business demonstrates high capital efficiency, evidenced by a 23.8% return on equity achieved in Q2 1994 [D06].

kill_criteria: Pricing power lost to persistent merchant fee resistance and competitive bank networks [D01], [D05]
Management fails to complete the divestiture of non-core, value-destructive assets [D03]
Credit losses exceed manageable historical bounds impairing capital ratios [D06]
final.what_would_change_our_mind: Evidence that the payments network's competitive advantage has been structurally eroded by fee pressure or that management has abandoned the strategy of shedding non-core assets.
final.memo:
The Company occupies a unique position in the world of commerce, providing a travel-payments franchise that acts as a vital bridge between cardholders and merchants [D01]. We have long understood the economics of this model, which relies on trust, scale, and the utility of a global service promise [D01]. 

This business is essentially a high-return, service-oriented franchise that requires little in the way of capital investment in plant or equipment [D01]. The travel-related services segment recently produced a 23.8% return on equity, showcasing the underlying power of the network [D06]. While the company has been distracted by its conglomerate past, the core payments business has consistently demonstrated its endurance [D01], [D03].

Management is now wisely refocusing the firm, shedding unrelated activities to concentrate on the payments and financial-services franchises [D01], [D03]. This shift is essential, as the market has been too focused on temporary volatility and past diversification woes to appreciate the strength of the core [D05].

At a price of $26.50, the company trades at an earnings yield of approximately 8.7%, based on 1993 continuing earnings of $2.30 per share [D02], [D04]. While we view the current valuation as fair, we are buying because the intrinsic value of this franchise will compound as the business is simplified [D03], [D04]. Like a fine painting, a wonderful business is worth paying a fair price for, and we are content to hold this interest indefinitely as the company continues to execute its strategy [D01], [D04].
